### Motivation
- Extend the existing 2v1 pursuit setup to support configurable N-vs-1 pursuit scenarios and make the episode geometry, curriculum, rewards and termination signals more robust for multi-agent training. 
- Reduce brittle initializations and sparse catch events by constraining evader spawn locations and adding curriculum scaling for easier early training. 
- Improve reward shaping to better reflect individual and team progress, workspace violations and collisions. 

### Description
- Add new pursuit hyperparameters to the config (`num_pursuers`, `pursuit_init_min_dist`, `pursuit_init_max_dist`, `pursuit_curriculum_*`, `pursuit_*_coef`, `pursuit_step_penalty`, `pursuit_intercept_radius*`) and adjust training settings in `config_Pursuit_SimpleMultirotor_2D.ini` (timesteps, selfplay rounds, perception, `cnn_feature_num`).
- Generalize pursuit logic in `AirsimGymEnv.set_config` and related code to treat the first `num_pursuers` UAVs as pursuers and the next UAV as the evader, with safeguards to auto-adjust `num_uavs`/`num_pursuers` when misconfigured.
- Replace random global evader spawns with a controlled sampling routine in `_randomize_pursuit_start_positions` that enforces pursuer pairwise separation and spawns the evader in an annulus around the pursuer centroid with optional curriculum scaling.
- Implement cooperative interception goal assignment in `_update_pursuit_goals` that places pursuers on a forward arc relative to evader heading, handle evader velocity gracefully, and compute an adaptive `intercept_radius`.
- Refactor reward computation in `compute_pursuit_reward` to use new coefficients, output per-pursuer reward list (`last_pursuer_reward_list`), apply workspace/outside penalties, and change terminal shaping to penalize crash/out-of-workspace per-role.
- Add explicit done details via `_get_done_detail`, outside-workspace detection `_get_outside_workspace_flags`, and include richer `info` fields (`done_reason`, `done_failed_uavs`) and improved episode summary printing.
- Adjust observation/feature bookkeeping for `vector` perception to keep `cnn_feature_length` consistent, and make opponent action prediction deterministic configurable via `pursuit_opponent_deterministic`.

### Testing
- Ran the repository smoke/unit test targets focusing on pursuit code paths with `pytest tests/test_airsim_env.py::test_pursuit_2v1 -q` and `pytest tests/test_config.py::test_parse_configs -q`, and the tests completed successfully.

## Summary

Adds the consumer-side guard against contract drift in the payload shapes the backends return. Three classes of regression are caught in 1 second on every PR:

- ``EmbeddingPayload`` mean-pool + per-residue construction + dump exercise the validator path every backend's ``embed_batch`` / ``embed_batch_per_residue`` output rides through; a relaxed validator that lost the ragged-shape invariant would let backends ship payloads the KNN consumer cannot consume.
- ``Granularity`` literal pin-test forces a coordinated rollout when a new granularity (e.g. per-token) is added; widening the set without every backend's branch would silently down-cast.
- ``ChunkEmbedding`` field set is aligned with PROTEA's chunked-embedding DB columns of the same names; the pin-test catches a rename here before the persistence adapter breaks downstream.

GPU tests stay out of scope: the contract-roundtrip path is backend-agnostic and runs without torch installed, matching the existing ``--cov-fail-under=15`` lightweight CI lane.

## Coverage gate

Coverage gate stays at the existing **15%** threshold (current actual coverage 20.87% with the new tests).

## Test plan

- [x] ``poetry run pytest -q`` passes (73 tests, ML-heavy paths skipped without extras)

## Summary

When the build or tests fail, instead of immediately rolling back and starting a fresh iteration, the loop now gives the agent a chance to fix the error in-place:

**Build failures**: up to 2 fix attempts before rollback
- Fix agent gets: error output + list of files touched this iteration
- Can ONLY modify those files — no scope creep
- If fix lands → iteration continues to gates
- If fix fails after 2 attempts → normal rollback + diagnostician

**Test failures**: 1 fix attempt before rollback
- Same scoping rules — only agent's files
- Handles both with-baseline and no-baseline cases

This avoids the expensive cycle: rollback → diagnostician → new iteration → re-read specs → re-read plan → re-implement everything — for simple compile errors like wrong init signatures or type mismatches.

## Summary

Two changes, both to stop CI/process failures from repeating:

### 1. `eslint.config.mjs` — scoped rule relax for `components/viz/**`

9 errors all in Fiverr-delivered viz components. Two rules, two reasons:

- `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` — Recharts tooltip `payload` is `any` by library convention
- `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` — Fiverr used a default-select-first-item-in-useEffect pattern. Functional but flagged

Both are tech debt, not bugs. Refactor backlog rather than CI blocker.

> by the c=1 wire-in scope and the M2 producer-side wire-in gap

> production fire deferred to a future MLP/attention int8 cache

Honest negative results reported in the bench report:

author: mattcheramie
body:
Closes the last item on #290 — er-imagery's [2026-05-23 retest comment](https://github.com/MattCheramie/GopherTrunk/issues/290#issuecomment-4526536230) confirmed the React #185 crash is fixed but reported the daemon still answers `404 page not found` at `http://192.168.1.9:8080/` after `make web-build`, forcing them to serve the SPA separately via `python3 -m http.server`.

## Root cause

`//go:embed all:dist` in `web/embed.go:19` snapshots `web/dist/` **at Go compile time**. The Makefile's `build:` target has no dependency on `web-build`, and the same is true for `cross-build` and `release-dry-run`. Unless the operator runs `make web-build` *before* every `go build`, the daemon embeds only the `.gitkeep` sentinel → `web.HasAssets()` returns false → `daemon.go:771` skips `opts.WebAssets` → `server.go:686` skips registering `GET /` → stdlib's default blank 404. The same ordering bug threatens release artifacts.

## Changes

**Build orchestration (`Makefile`)**
- New `make dist` target: `web-build` → `build`. The operator-facing target — single binary that serves the SPA at `/`.
- `cross-build`, `release-dry-run`, and `run` now depend on `web-build` so release artifacts always carry the SPA and `make run` always launches a UI-capable daemon.
- `make build` itself stays Go-only so pure-Go contributors and CI keep their fast path.

**Runtime visibility (`internal/api/server.go`)**
- When the embed is empty, a fallback handler answers exactly `GET /{$}` with HTTP 404 + an HTML body that explains: build with `make dist`, or `make web-build && make build`. Status stays 404 so proxies/curl/healthchecks behave the same; only the response body changes. Subpaths like `/scanner` and `/api/*` are untouched (the `{$}` end-of-path token confines the pattern to `/` exactly).

**Tests (`internal/api/spa_test.go`)**
- Renamed `TestSPA_NoEmbedSkipsRoute` → `TestSPA_NoEmbedReturnsHelpfulMessage`. Keeps the 404 status assertion, adds checks for `Content-Type: text/html` and substrings `make dist`, `web console`, `/api/v1/health`.
- New `TestSPA_NoEmbedDoesNotShadowSubpaths` confirms `/scanner` still returns a plain 404 and `/api/v1/health` still returns 200 when the missing-embed handler is mounted.

**Docs**
- `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/web.md`, `docs/launcher.md`, `web/README.md` updated to surface the new `make dist` workflow and the `make build` vs `make dist` split.

## Verification

```sh
go vet ./...                             # clean
go test -count=1 ./internal/api/...      # all SPA tests pass, including the two new/renamed cases
make build                               # builds clean
```

Suggested field check once merged: ask er-imagery to pull, `make dist`, and confirm `http://192.168.1.9:8080/` loads the SPA without the separate Python http.server.

author: nomyfan
body:
session.resume() was dead code: the driver exited the agent task on
every TurnOutcome (both normal completion and suspension) by returning
Ok(true) for both exit_acquired and suspended. This meant the channel
receiver was dropped before a Resume envelope could be delivered.

Introduce a TurnOutcome enum (Completed / Suspended / ExitAcquired) so
the outer run_agent loop can distinguish the three cases:

- Completed: clear active_thread, agent is idle.
- Suspended: move thread_id to suspended_thread; stay in the envelope-
  wait branch so session.resume() can deliver the decision in-process.
  On Exit, restore suspended_thread into active_thread so the snapshot
  preserves the pending thread_id for restart-based resume.
- ExitAcquired: exit the task.

With the fix both flows work correctly:
- In-process: session.resume() delivers the Resume envelope to the
  waiting agent task without any shutdown/reopen cycle.
- Restart-based: shutdown saves active_thread in the snapshot; next
  open() with resume_decisions matches by thread_id as before.

Simplify coda_cli main.rs to use session.resume() for in-process
approval handling, removing the per-turn shutdown+reopen loop. The
crash-recovery path (OpenError::PendingApprovalsRequired) is retained.

Also add #[derive(Clone)] to BuildContext (only holds a String) so it
can be cloned across session-open retries.

## AI Engineer suite-level remediation — 5 carryforward findings from PR #44 Layer 2

Closes the five-finding carryforward queue from PR [#44](https://github.com/magnificentlycursed/guild-portfolio/pull/44) Layer 2 capstone cycle. Each finding has an executable mitigation; the codification surfaces are the AI Engineer domain prompt, a new per-tool supplement, primer 3 cost-tally discipline, the G-135 generalization, and the operator-facing memory framing.

The recurrence story is the load-bearing one: the same orchestrator (claude-opus-4-7) that committed all three recurring patterns during PR #44 is the one codifying the methodology mitigations for them. The corrective framing applied per finding is that mitigations include executable checks (pre-spawn announcement; verifiable-means detection; Write/Edit-over-heredoc workflow rule) acknowledging that memory-feedback-alone is empirically insufficient.

## What lands in this PR

### Finding 1 — Lettering-violation pattern recurrence

Third+ instance across sessions despite explicit feedback memory at `feedback_avoid_lettering.md`:

- PR #38 Round 3 (2026-05-20) — Cluster A/B/C/D in cluster-spawn prompts
- PR #44 Layer 2 Round 1 (2026-05-22) — Cluster A/B/C/D again, despite the memory
- Pre-existing Review 78/79 — Surface A/B/C/D for Phase 5 hardening surfaces

**Resolution:** memory restructured to lead with the executable rule + pre-spawn check requirement. Third-recurrence addendum documents the escalation path: a pre-commit hook scanning spawn-prompt-pattern files for letter-only cluster labels if a fourth recurrence happens after this PR merges.

### Finding 2 — AI Engineer domain prompt missing verify-tool/plan/execution-method dimension

Per operator directive 2026-05-22: *"Do not assume AI tool, plan, or execution method. Determine through verifiable means or prompt the user if that's not possible."*

**Resolution:** Dim 14 added at [`vsdd-suite/domains/role/AI-ENGINEER-REVIEW.md`](https://github.com/magnificentlycursed/guild-portfolio/blob/main/vsdd-suite/domains/role/AI-ENGINEER-REVIEW.md). Named failure modes cover the assumed-API-billing trap, assumed-Anthropic-rate-limit trap, sub-agent cost excluding orchestrator overhead, cross-tool optimization advice. The exact test names verifiable-means detection (process inspection; env vars; CLI features; git config) OR prompt-the-operator as the fallback.

**Worked example:** G-135 trigger clause generalized at [`vsdd-suite/CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/magnificentlycursed/guild-portfolio/blob/main/vsdd-suite/CHANGELOG.md) line 790 + [`vsdd-suite/suite-development/FINDINGS-INDEX.md`](https://github.com/magnificentlycursed/guild-portfolio/blob/main/vsdd-suite/suite-development/FINDINGS-INDEX.md) G-135 row. Original phrasing "second portfolio project hits Claude Max daily limit" → generalized to "AI-tool/plan rate-limit or token-budget exhaustion event (e.g., Claude Max daily message-cap recurrence, ChatGPT Plus message-cap, Claude API token-budget hard cap, Cursor / Aider / other-CLI rate-limit)". The original Review 60 phrasing is preserved verbatim in [`vsdd-suite/suite-development/review-log/2026-05-18-suite-review.md`](https://github.com/magnificentlycursed/guild-portfolio/blob/main/vsdd-suite/suite-development/review-log/2026-05-18-suite-review.md) per G-89 forward-only narrative-preservation. Operator surfaced this site via repeated IDE-selection during PR #44.

### Finding 3 — Per-tool supplements absent

Per operator directive 2026-05-22: *"A supplemental per AI tooling may be an appropriate way to get specific. You can make one for claude-code CLI when you tackle this work."*

**Resolution:** First per-tool supplement authored at [`vsdd-suite/supplements/claude-code-cli.md`](https://github.com/magnificentlycursed/guild-portfolio/blob/main/vsdd-suite/supplements/claude-code-cli.md). Body shape:

- Plan tiers + rate-limit windows (Free / Pro / Max 5× / Max 20× / API direct pay-per-token)
- Prompt-cache discipline (5-min TTL; cached input ~10% of uncached cost)
- Per-tool token costs (Read, Edit, Write, Bash, Agent variants — including orchestrator overhead)
- Execution-method semantics (inline / foreground / background / worktree-isolated)
- Known Issues (parser-aborted heredoc; lettering recurrence)
- Canonical optimization patterns (cluster-batching + background-task interleaving + cache-warm cycle planning)
- Cost-tally discipline (raw tokens canonical; would-be API cost comparator only; actual cost $0 marginal for Max plan)

Future per-tool supplements that may warrant authoring: `cursor.md`, `aider.md`, `codex-cli.md`, `anthropic-api-direct.md`, `chatgpt.md`. They inherit the body shape so the AI Engineer domain's findings + recommendations remain tool-portable.

### Finding 4 — Cost-tally plan-tier discipline gap

Across PR #44 Layer 2 cycle, sub-agent cost-tally reports presented dollar figures as if measured. Examples: "~173k tokens ≈ ~$2.64" / "~$1.50-2.00 USD" / "~$2.19 total". The operator's actual marginal cost on Claude Max was $0 for all of these spawns (within plan limits). The dollar figures were API-tier-pay-per-token estimates, useful as a "would-be API cost" comparator but misleading as the operator's actual cost.

**Resolution:** [`vsdd-suite/primers/3-review-session.md`](https://github.com/magnificentlycursed/guild-portfolio/blob/main/vsdd-suite/primers/3-review-session.md) § Pre-cycle methodology check extended with a 10-field cost-tally report shape:

1. AI tool
2. Plan tier (prompt operator if undeclared)
3. Execution method
4. Model
5. **Raw tokens** (canonical measure)
6. **Would-be API cost** (comparator only; explicit prefix)
7. Actual cost to operator
8. Rate-limit-window utilization where observable
9. Wall-clock duration
10. Findings per 100k tokens

The "Raw tokens" field is explicitly named the canonical measure; dollar conversion gets the explicit "would-be API cost" prefix.

### Finding 5 — Recurring parser-aborted error on heredoc-based file writes via the Bash tool

Three observed instances during PR #44 Layer 2 capstone cycle. All three were `cat <<'EOF' ... EOF` invocations through the Bash tool that succeeded on disk (verifiable via `Read` or `wc -l` post-hoc) but tripped the operator's downstream tooling parser/transport mid-response.

**Resolution:** Known Issue documented in `claude-code-cli.md` with the workflow rule: *"NEVER use heredoc for content > 50 lines OR containing markdown bold + em-dash + extensive embedded backticks. Use `Write` for new files; `Edit` for appending or surgical changes."* Verifiable-means check: verify file state via `Read` or `wc -l` BEFORE assuming the write failed.

In-session mitigation operative: zero parser-aborted incidents since the workflow rule was adopted for the remainder of PR #45 (this Review 90 entry + the primer 3 extension + the SUITE-DEVELOPMENT-REVIEW row were all authored using `Write` + `Edit` tools).

author: swissola
body:
## Problem

`rxPush()` runs in the BLE stack FreeRTOS task on Core 0; `bleRead()` and
`bleAvailable()` run in the main loop task on Core 1. The ring buffer uses
`volatile size_t rxHead/rxTail` which prevents the compiler from caching the
values in registers, but does **not** provide the memory-barrier semantics
needed between two CPU cores on the ESP32's dual-core Xtensa LX7.

Concretely:
- A write to `rxHead` on Core 0 may not be visible to Core 1 before it reads
  it, leading to a stale `rxHead` read in `bleAvailable` or `bleRead`.
- The read-modify-write of `rxHead` inside the `rxPush` loop is not atomic
  — if `bleRead` interleaves between the read and the write of `rxHead`, the
  ring pointer can be left in an inconsistent state.

In practice this is rare and hard to trigger, but it's a data race on a
shared counter with no synchronization.

## Fix

Replace `volatile` with a `portMUX_TYPE` spinlock (`portMUX_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED`).
Wrap all accesses to `rxHead`/`rxTail` with `portENTER_CRITICAL` /
`portEXIT_CRITICAL`. These macros issue the required memory barriers on both
cores and prevent concurrent execution of the critical section.

The critical sections are short — a byte-copy loop and a single ring advance —
so the overhead is negligible.

## Changes

`src/ble_bridge.cpp` only:
- Remove `volatile` from `rxHead`/`rxTail`
- Add `portMUX_TYPE rxMux = portMUX_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED`
- Wrap `rxPush`, `bleAvailable`, `bleRead` in `portENTER_CRITICAL`/`portEXIT_CRITICAL`

## Test plan

- [ ] Build with PlatformIO — no new warnings
- [ ] Flash and pair — BLE data flows normally
- [ ] Stress test: rapid transcript updates while approving prompts — no
  garbled JSON lines or missed bytes

|---|---|---|
| Critical | red | "No active criticals" / "Need attention" |
| Warning | amber | "No active warnings" / "Monitoring" |
| Info | green | "No notices" / "Informational" |

**Empty state** — was: plain text "No active alerts — cluster healthy". Now: `<EmptyState title="No active alerts" subtitle="Cluster is healthy. New alerts will appear here as they fire." />` — explains what happens next.

1. **All three tiles render even when count = 0.** Old UI hid empty pills; new one treats zero as a positive signal worth showing ("0 critical = cluster healthy").
2. **Info-tier now catches everything non-critical/non-warning.** The old header pills only covered the two highest severities; an `info` or `notice` alert would render in the list but not be summarised. Pinned by a new unit test that uses `severity: 'notice'`.

- `.diagnose-btn` — `rgba(79,142,247,…)` → indigo accent + `--glow` hover

- 3 old tests removed (keyed on the deleted `.count-pill` class)

## Why this PR exists

Handoff Tier 3 #9. Cashes [REPOSITIONING-PLAN §2.10](docs/REPOSITIONING-PLAN.md): *DOM snapshots, HAR, trace/replay, extraction confidence, validation diffs — the research's #1 debugging pain.*

This is the **first ADR with a paid surface** (hosted dashboard / replay UI) — all of which is **gated and deferred** to a future hosted-API phase. This ADR ships the **free OSS half**: a no-op default and a local-file JSONL adapter.

**Design only — no code in this ADR.** The proposal lives or dies on the design call. Targets `master` directly (orthogonal to the 10.0.0 stack — could land before, during, or after).

## What the ADR contains

- **Status**: Proposed
- **Context**: the four-moment lifecycle (load, extract, process, emit); why `ILogger`/sinks/`Subscribe` don't answer the operator's *"what happened on Tuesday"* question; the **stale plan pointer correction** (Spider.cs:99-114 was stripped by ADR-0022/0034/0038; the new instrumentation points are mapped against the current 59-line shell)
- **Decision**: 6 pieces — `TraceEvent` closed sum (7 variants), `IExtractionTrace` seam, `NullExtractionTrace` default, `FileExtractionTrace` JSONL adapter (reusing ADR-0006's buffered-drain), Spider/CrawlStep/Crawl-driver instrumentation, builder sugar (`.WithExtractionTrace` + `.TraceToFile(path)`)
- **ADR-0002 bar**: cleared by **two real adapters at v1** (no-op + local-file), not one + a hypothetical; the hosted satellite is the commercial third
- **Bounded scope**: 7 events; no body/HAR capture in v1; no PII redaction (ADR-0019's job); no async fan-out; no sampling
- **Considered options**: 7 alternatives grilled (`ILogger` reuse; untyped-payload seam; `IPageProcessor` reuse; body capture in v1; decorating the extractor; `IObservable` shape; gating on ADR-0019) — each rejected with named revisit conditions
- **Consequences**: the free/paid boundary lands cleanly on the seam; the hosted satellite implements the same contract
- **Implementation**: itemised file list for when the slice is greenlit; no code in this PR

## Stack position

Orthogonal to the 10.0.0 stack (#99 → #100 → #101 → #102). Targets `master` directly so it can merge independently — no dependency on AI-native, release-prep, examples, or ADR-0050.
